sourceNote: The mesh of the user of 2026-10-16 (assets/models/cat/README.md), with new faces on each arm. The user said on 2026-10-24: "note that there's significant twisting happening for the arms and wrists. add loop edges and retopology and additional bones if needed to address them". The upper arm of the user mesh joins the side of the trunk down to the elbow, so the new faces also make an armpit: a cut along the seam where the arm meets the trunk, a side wall of the trunk under the arm, and a quad tube whose flat inner side lies on the wall and meets it only at the armpit line. tools/blender/cat_arms.py replays the Blender session that made it. The faces of the paws, the trunk, the legs, and the head are the faces of the user. The user said "make the cat's belly more oval and smooth" on 2026-10-27, so the trunk of the copy moves to an even oval from the front and from the side (step_belly() of the script), with its faces and colors. The user said "the cat's arm has lumps" on 2026-10-27, and the play showed the flat side wall under the arm as a light patch with a crease, so the side wall has even faces with no lips of the seam cut under it, and the trunk near it rounds into it (step_round_wall() of the script, docs/decisions/2026-10-28-cat-wall.md). The file of the user, cat.glb, stays unchanged.
paintedNote: The weights of the arm tubes are the automatic weights of Blender with the Weight Paint fixes of tools/blender/cat_arms.py. The trunk, the side walls, the socket of each arm, and the first ring of each shoulder hang only on the bones of paintedLower after the fixes, so they keep the rule weights of weights: the shoulder turns with the rules of the user mesh. With Blender weights on the chest, the faces of the chest in front of each shoulder turned over in the play.

armSegments.note: Each upper arm and each forearm has 4 deform segments, and each elbow and wrist a helper bone of this length in units, as on the rabbit. The app turns them from the joints of the pose (poseArm() of src/models/studio-rig.ts). They replace the rings of refine.

rootNormals.note: The skin faces whose middle lies within radius (units) of the head of an upper arm take the normals of the skin with no crease angle in the app (root_rim() of tools/blender/rig_mesh.py), as on the fox and the deer. The bind turns the arm root, and the crease angle 35 split the normals at the back of each arm root into hard dark lines from behind and to the left, at rest and in the play, with no dark color (user, 2026-10-27: "the cat's arm has dent", docs/research/2026-10-27-cat-fox.md).

name: Cat

app.note: The scale puts the standing ear tips 1.758 m above the floor, the ear tips of the red fox of the app, because the user chose the size of the fox on 2026-10-16 ("1.76 m, as the fox"). The leg factor 1.5 raised the ear tips from 1 to 1.0725 units, so the scale is 1.639161 m for each unit (docs/research/2026-10-16-cat-mesh/arm-factors-legs.txt). The scale stays 1.639161 m for each unit since then. The trunk factor of 2026-10-17 keeps the legs, so the cat is shorter: the standing shoulder joints are 0.636146 units, 1.042745 m, above the floor, and the depth factor raises them to 0.636239 units, 1.042897 m (keptHeight() of tools/rig-mesh.ts, docs/research/2026-10-16-cat-form/). At the shoulder joints of the parametric cat of main (0.55233 m), the cat was 0.868 m high to the ear tips (landmark-probe.txt). The reach is the reach of the shorter arms of cat-arms.glb, 0.4128 m from the left shoulder joint to the middle of the palm (0.4791 m with the arms of the user mesh): the user said "the cat's arm ... is longer than expected" on 2026-10-27 (docs/decisions/2026-10-27-cat-fox2.md), and "the cats arms are too long" on 2026-10-26 of the reach of the red fox (0.5452 m). The cat plays a smaller viola for the shorter arms, and its hold puts the viola nearer to the neck, so that the left paw reaches the nut. With no --check, pnpm rig-mesh stops when the reach is more than 1% from this reach.

armFactorNote: The factor of the upper arm and the forearm in the rig: 1, because the rig with arm segments does not stretch the arms. The upper arm of cat-arms.glb is 0.92 and the forearm 0.78 as long as on the user mesh (the factors of step_shape() of tools/blender/cat_arms.py), 1.10 head heights from the shoulder joint to the wrist (1.30 before), so that the forearm is 0.86 of the upper arm, with the cross-section 0.85 of the user mesh (the armGirth of 2026-10-17: the user said that the arms of the cat "seem too muscular"). The user said on 2026-10-27: "the cat's arm has dent and is longer than expected" (docs/decisions/2026-10-27-cat-fox2.md). The shoulder joint below is the joint of the user mesh, and the elbow, the wrist, and the paw joints move with the shorter bones (arm-joints.py of docs/research/2026-10-27-cat-fox2/probes/). pnpm rig-mesh cat --check measures the reach 0.4128 m at the scale of app.shoulders (app.reach). With the arms of the user mesh (0.4791 m), the trunk of the cat, 0.69 of the trunk of the mesh, made the arm reach the crotch when it hangs. From 2026-10-25 to 2026-10-26, the arms were 1.1496 times longer, for the reach of the red fox (0.5452 m), and the user said "the cats arms are too long" (docs/decisions/2026-10-26-third-review.md).
legFactorNote: The factor of the thigh and the shin. Each one stretches only between its joints, the foot keeps its size, and the body rises 0.1365 units, so that the soles stay at y 0. The user chose the longer legs of the fox on 2026-10-16 ("Longer legs, 1.5x"): with the factor 1, the thigh was 0.075 units long and the seat 0.075 m high at the shoulder joints of the parametric cat. With the trunk factor 0.85768 of 2026-10-16, the legs grew until the standing ear tips stayed at 1.758 m: 1.5 + (1 - 0.85768) × 0.45 / 0.145 = 1.94168, where 0.45 units is the height of the neck joint above the hips joint and 0.145 units the height of the hip joint above the ankle (docs/decisions/2026-10-16-cat-trunk.md). The shorter trunk of 2026-10-17 keeps these legs.
neckFactorNote: The factor of the neck between its joints. The head keeps its size and moves down the neck with the head joint. The user said that the necks of the cat and the fox are too long on 2026-10-16, and the manager chose 0.65, the factor of the fox (docs/decisions/2026-10-16-cat-form.md): the neck joint is 4.9 cm from the head joint (7.6 cm before), and the chin is 0.257 H above the shoulder joints (0.341 H before, the red fox 0.288 H).
girthFactorNote: The factors of the width and of the depth of the trunk and of the clavicles across the trunk axis (girth_moves() of tools/blender/rig_mesh.py). The user said that the cat "seems too skinny" on 2026-10-16, and the manager chose the width 1.08 and the depth 1.15, so that the trunk meets the sheet docs/reference/cat-views.png (docs/decisions/2026-10-16-cat-form.md). In head heights, the belly is 1.420, the hips 1.473, and the depth 1.308, against 1.400, 1.448, and 1.296 on the sheet (1.275, 1.345, and 1.123 before). The arms, the legs, and the tail keep their sizes and move out with their joints (docs/research/2026-10-16-cat-form/).
trunkFactorNote: The factor of the trunk between the hips joint and the neck joint (trunk_moves() of tools/blender/rig_mesh.py). The user said "the cat is too long and its chair is too low" on 2026-10-16, and chose the trunk of the red fox ("V2, fox trunk", the factor 0.85768): the standing trunk from the hips joint to the shoulder joints was 0.597 m. Then the user said "the cat's body is too long and it seems too skinny", and the manager chose 0.8 of that trunk, 0.686144 (docs/decisions/2026-10-16-cat-form.md): the trunk is 0.475 m, and from the narrowest neck row to the crotch it is 1.76 head heights, as on the red fox (1.76). The legs keep their length. The head, the arms, the legs, and the tail keep their sizes and move with the trunk. The factor 0.9 of that trunk gave 1.98 head heights (docs/research/2026-10-16-cat-form/).
jointsNote: The places are in the units and the axes of the studio in the pose of the source: 1 unit from the soles to the ear tips, the soles at y = 0, +z forward, +x the left side. The right side mirrors the left side. The probes are in docs/research/2026-10-16-cat-mesh/. sections.py gives the cuts at each height (sections-y.txt): the feet below y 0.04 (the toes forward to z 0.135), the thin shins from 0.045 to 0.105, the wide thighs from 0.11 to the crotch at 0.19, the body from 0.19 to 0.52 with the round belly forward to z 0.178, the shoulders from 0.525 (x ±0.172) to 0.655, the narrow neck at 0.685 to 0.705 (x ±0.06), the head from 0.705 with the muzzle to z 0.224, and the ears apart from 0.915. The trunk joints lie 0.01 to 0.02 behind the middle of the body cut, as in the fox, from the hips over the crotch to the chest 0.086 below the shoulder joint. The thigh joint lies at the crotch, a little behind the middle of the leg cut, the knee where the thin shin meets the wide thigh, the ankle where the foot starts, and the toes at the ball of the foot. The ear joint lies on the line of the middles of the ear cuts at 0.915 and 0.955, at the top of the head (0.89), and its tail at the ear tip. The cuts across the axis of the free arm (arm-axis.txt) give its middle line, which leaves the body between x 0.083 and 0.087. The shoulder joint lies on that line, 0.025 inside the root (x 0.06). The wrist of the user mesh lies at the narrowest cut, where the paw starts (s -0.02 to -0.01), the elbow halfway from the shoulder joint to the wrist and 0.01 behind the line, and the finger joint at the knuckles, 0.03 before the tip of the paw. The tail is a chain of two bones (sections-y.txt and sections-z.txt). The tail joint lies at the middle of the root of the tail, between its top on the back (y 0.35, z -0.04) and its bottom on the thighs (y 0.24, z -0.026). The tail hangs straight down to the bend at y 0.08, and its end goes back along the floor to the tip (y 0.03, z -0.215). The tail_tip joint lies at the bend, 0.223 units from the root. Each roll is the hint of the z axis of the bone, forward by default. The arm bones take the normal of the palm (palm): the smallest principal direction of the vertices of the left paw, inward and down (facts.txt).

studio.trunkNote: The trunk of the seated bind sits upright (trunk_turn() of tools/blender/rig_mesh.py): the pelvis turns back around the head of the hips until the hip angle from the side opens by open degrees, and each trunk bone takes its share of that turn as its world turn. The trunk axis of the cat from the hip joints to the neck joint is vertical in the source. So with open 0, it leans 0.6 degrees forward in the play pose, and with open 3, the value of the red fox, it leans 2.4 degrees back (docs/research/2026-10-16-cat-mesh/hip-probe-open0.txt and hip-probe-open3.txt). With open 1, it leans 0.4 degrees back (hip-probe.txt), and no face turns over after the crease. With open 0, the crease turned over 4 faces. The shares are the shares of the fox and the rabbit.
studio.bindArmsNote: The bind upper arm points 38 degrees from the hanging upper arm of the mesh, (0.568, -0.822, 0.037), as the bind upper arm of the deer (docs/decisions/2026-10-26-fifth-review-deer.md). With the bind arm of the other meshes, 53 degrees from it, the seated bind turned the arm root far from the mesh: the lower back of the socket and the armpit line folded into a crease with dark slivers at the back of the upper arm near the shoulder, at rest and in the play (user, 2026-10-27: "the cat's arm has dent", docs/research/2026-10-27-cat-fox.md). With (0.62, -0.62, 0.48), 28 degrees from it, the left twist p95 of pnpm arm-check went from 26 to 39 and the right flat p5 from 0.84 to 0.75.
studio.bindSupinationNote: The bind paw of the left arm turns 120 degrees about its bind forearm toward supination (paw_supination() of tools/blender/rig_mesh.py), and the forearm segments share the turn in the bind. The forearm of the app turns with its elbow hinge, so the bind paw sets the zero of the paw twist. With the bind arms alone, the left paw of the viola twisted -94 degrees at rest and 118 to 151 degrees in the play, and it supinated through 180 degrees in each lift and lowering, where the forearm skin unwound. With 120 degrees, it twists 26 degrees at rest and -122 to -89 degrees in the play. The forearm twist p95 of pnpm arm-check was 64, 60, 55, and 50 with 90, 100, 110, and 120 degrees (66 with no turn), and each turn removed the folds of the left paw in the play (docs/decisions/2026-10-27-left-paw-bind.md). With 90 degrees, the play twist reached -152 degrees. The right paw holds the bow and keeps the bind arms.

tailCurl.note: The seated tail curls on the seat around the left side of the haunch, on the side of the viola, as a sitting cat curls its tail (the variant T1 that the user chose on 2026-10-16, docs/decisions/2026-10-16-cat-seat.md). The points are the places of the curve after the root of the tail in the seated bind, in units from the root (curl_line() of tools/blender/rig_mesh.py): down and to the left behind the haunch, forward along the left side of the haunch at the seat top, and the tip up and in over the left thigh. Each vertex moves by the smoothstep of its tail share from 0.5 to 0.95, so that the root of the tail stays with the haunch. The haunch is 18 to 21 cm wide on each side of the middle and the seat 21 cm, so the tail lies 11.8 cm outside the side edge of the seat at most. The tail goes 0.5 cm into the body at most, 0.1 cm into the left back post of the chair of the app, and 0.0 cm into the seat (docs/research/2026-10-16-cat-seat/). The trunk factor lowers the root of the tail 1.3 cm closer to the seat top, and the tail goes 0.4 cm into the seat top in the rig, and 0.0 cm into the seat, 0.3 cm into the body, and 0.0 cm into the back posts in the app. A lift of the points by 0.0008 units or more raised the side view of the haunch from 0.13 cm to 1.9 cm (docs/research/2026-10-16-cat-trunk/). The shorter and deeper trunk of 2026-10-17 lowers the root of the tail and moves it back, and the tail went 1.56 cm into the seat top of the rig. So each point is 0.006 units higher, and the tail goes 0.38 cm into the seat top of the rig. With 8 rounds of smoothing of the sit, the lift does not raise the haunch (docs/research/2026-10-16-cat-form/seat-fit.txt). Two straight bones cannot lie on the seat: the root bone is 36.6 cm long.

studio.note: The studio has no cat. legTurns gives the world turn of each left leg bone from the seated bind pose to the source, and the right side mirrors it. The user asked for a taller chair and legs more perpendicular to the floor on 2026-10-16, and the manager chose the posture P25 (docs/decisions/2026-10-16-cat-form.md): the thigh slopes 25 degrees down from the hip to the knee, 8 degrees out, and the shin is vertical, with the ankle under the knee, so that the knee angle from the side is 115 degrees. The foot and the toes keep the turn of the source, so that the soles stand flat on the floor (docs/research/2026-10-16-hip-open/leg_turns.py <config> 25 8 0). The source shin slants 2.5 degrees back. The seat of 2026-10-16 had the thigh 15 degrees down and the shin 23.8 degrees forward of vertical, with the ankles 9.0 cm in front of the knees (docs/research/2026-10-16-cat-trunk/seat-probe.txt). The bind arms are the bind arms of the fox and the rabbit. tailCurl gives the seated tail. With the hanging tail of tailBind (the root back over the seat 20 degrees below the level, the tip back and down behind the chair), the tail passed the back posts of the chair of the app and its end was 11.7 cm above the floor (docs/decisions/2026-10-16-mesh-cat.md).

weights.armSplitNote: With the rebuilt arms, the side wall under each arm and the socket lie inside the plane |x| = 0.1 (0.085 before), and below the armpit line at the height 0.6 they keep no arm weight (armBelow). With 0.085, the rules gave the side wall the weights of the free arm, and the wall followed the arm as a flap on the back.
weights.stretchRampNote: With a ramp, the upper arm stretches by the arm factor only on the free arm: the share of the stretch fades from 0 to 1 over this many units on each side of the plane |x| = armSplit. 0 gives no ramp, as for the fox and the rabbit.

noseFront.note: The tips of the lower whiskers hang below headFrom, down to y 0.6956, in front of the plane z = front, and only they lie there (17 vertices). With the weights of the neck, the head lift of the play bent each lower whisker at the head line, and faces 4220 and 4223 turned over in each play sample (2026-10-27-cat3 decisions). With the plane 0.17, the rule also took the front of the belly. The head measures leave the tips out (headFloor of tools/studio-body.ts).

sliver.note: The corners of each thin face share one set of weights, so that the face moves rigidly and does not turn over at a bent joint. A thin face has a corner angle below angle (degrees) and a longest edge below longest (units). The angle is the angle of the fox and the rabbit. The longest edge was 0.03 units, as for the fox and the rabbit, until the arm girth factors of 2026-10-17: then face 1248 of the left armpit, a thin face of 6.0 degrees with a longest edge of about 0.037 units, turned over in each rest sample and in 2.0% of the play samples. With 0.04 units, its corners share one set of weights and it does not fold. The rule takes 228 faces in 21 groups. Face 73 of the right wrist then folds in 3.3% of the play samples. 0.035 units kept face 1248 and folded face 73, and 0.05 units folded the right paw in 71% of the play samples (docs/research/2026-10-17-cat-look/).

line.note: The middle corner of each long thin face (a corner angle above angle, in degrees) takes the mix of the weights of its two other corners by its place along their line, so that it does not lag behind the line when a joint bends. With head, the corners of the head take the rule too. The values are the values of the fox. The rule takes 172 corners.

weights.clavicleFromNote: The share of the clavicle weight that a vertex keeps grows from 0 at the lower height to 1 at the upper height (units), and the chest takes the rest. This is the rule of the fox, moved with the clavicle joint of the cat (y 0.645 against 0.635), so that a small face of the chest does not take a clavicle weight that the bow arm turns far.
weights.armTopNote: The share of the weight of the clavicles and of the upper arms that a vertex keeps falls from 1 at the lower height to 0 at the upper height (units), and the neck takes the rest. The shoulders of the cat end at y 0.655, and the neck is narrowest at 0.685 to 0.705 (sections-y.txt). The rule of the fox keeps a raised bow arm from a drag of the side of the neck. With 0.655 to 0.7, the right shoulder turn of 36 degrees (CAT_HOLD.reach) folded faces 820, 821, and 1046 at the right clavicle and the neck under the chin in 82% to 100% of the play: their clavicle corners (0.76 to 0.98) swung past the neck corner beside them. With 0.645 to 0.69, they fold in no sample, the most folded faces of a play sample go from 28 to 27, and the pits at the back of the left arm root are 4.2 cubic cm in the play (4.8 before), but 21.5 at the right root (20.5). With 0.64 to 0.69, the right root had 24.9, and with 0.65 to 0.695, face 821 still folded in 3% of the play (docs/research/2026-10-27-cat-lap.md).
weights.shoulderRampNote: Above the heights of y (units), the share of the upper arm weight that a vertex keeps grows from 0 at the distance x[0] from the middle plane to 1 at x[1], and the clavicle of its side takes the rest. The cat has narrow shoulders under a thin neck, and bone heat gave 0.93 of the weight of vertices on top of the right shoulder next to the neck to the upper arm. Faces 187, 204, 205, and 250 from these vertices to the neck turned over in each sample of the violist (pnpm fold-probe violist). x starts at the neck (x 0.06) and ends past the root of the arm (x 0.087 to 0.13 in the cuts of sections-x.txt), and y starts at the top of the root of the arm. With this ramp, faces 187, 205, and 250 do not fold in the play, and the other faces of the top of the right shoulder fold in at most 18% of the play samples (face 162, docs/research/2026-10-16-cat-mesh/rig-mesh-check-cat-shoulder-ramp.log, hold-fit-violist-candidate.log). A lower armTop (0.6 to 0.66) gave the outer top of the shoulder to the neck, and a face there folded in each sample. A shoulder joint lower and further out (0.085 to 0.09 units out, 0.58 to 0.6 units up) folded other faces in each sample (rig-mesh-check-cat-fold-variants-1.log and -2.log, rig-mesh-check-cat-joint-variants.log).
weights.shoulderHeadNote: Below headFrom, the share of the head weight that goes to the neck grows from 0 at the smaller distance from the middle plane to all at the larger distance (units). The values are the values of the fox, scaled by the neck of the cat (x ±0.06 against ±0.089).
weights.fingersNote: The fingers keep this share of their bone heat weight, and the hand takes the rest, as in the fox and the rabbit.

haunch.note: The part of the thigh weight that goes to the hips grows from 0 at the lower height to 1 at the upper height, so that the buttocks stay on the hips and the thigh turns onto the seat. This is the ramp of the fox (0.16 to 0.27), scaled by the thigh of the cat: it starts 0.025 units above the knee and ends 0.03 units above the thigh joint. The thigh of the cat is 0.075 units long, and the thigh of the fox 0.105.

weights.note: Beyond the plane |x| = armSplit, only the free arm follows the arm bones: the cuts of sections.py x show the arm apart from the body from x 0.087 out (sections-x.txt). Above headFrom, each vertex except the ears follows the head only: the neck is narrowest at y 0.685 to 0.705, and the chin starts at 0.705. The whiskers follow the head. Each ear vertex goes to its ear bone with a ramp over the heights of earBase. The tail has two bones (tail): the vertices within radius of the line from the root over the bend to the tip, and behind the plane z = behind, follow the tail bones. The share of the tail bones grows from 0 to 1 over the places of root along the line (units from the root), the share of the tip within the tail grows from 0 to 1 over bend units on each side of the bend, and the share of the tail bones takes the mean of its neighbors in smooth rounds. The radius holds each cut of the tail (x ±0.037 at most, facts.txt), and the plane keeps the backs of the thighs (z -0.025 at y 0.235) out of it. The rule takes 127 vertices, and 193 vertices have a tail weight after the smooth rounds.

refine.ringsNote: No ring: the quad tube of each arm has rings at the elbow and the wrist (tools/blender/cat_arms.py). Before the rebuilt arms of 2026-10-25, a ring at each elbow and wrist cut 18 edges of the user mesh (docs/research/2026-10-16-cat-mesh/rig-mesh-check-cat-rings.log).

flip.note: The long edge of a face of the arms with a corner angle above angle (degrees) in the seated bind mesh flips to the corner of the face on its other side, when the two faces lie almost on one plane (normals, degrees) and the surface moves at most move (units). The values are the values of the fox and the rabbit. The rule flips 8 edges, with a move of at most 1.28 mm (rig-mesh-check-cat-final.log).

pointFlip.note: The edge at this point is the diagonal of one quad of the tube at the inner right elbow (point_flips() of tools/blender/rig_mesh.py), the long edge of face 488 (corners 18, 140, and 22 degrees in the bind). With the shorter arms and the viola nearer to the body of 2026-10-27, the bow elbow bends further, and this thin face folded in 71% of the play samples. With the other diagonal, it folds in no sample (docs/research/2026-10-27-cat-fox2.md).

check.note: pnpm rig-mesh --check lists the faces of the seated bind mesh with a corner angle below angle (degrees) and a longest edge of at least length (units), when that edge passes within near (units) of a joint of the arms or the legs. These faces are candidates for a ring (refine.rings). The values are the values of the fox and the rabbit.

tone.note: The warm stage light gives the gray fur and the cream belly of the mesh four times the Oklab chroma of their faces: a front render of the gallery had the fur at chroma 0.061 and the belly at 0.065, against 0.016 and 0.020 on the sheet. The user chose the half step on 2026-10-16 ("Half step", docs/decisions/2026-10-16-cat-seat.md): each face of the plain fur moves half of the way of the full step, which gave the sheet medians in the gallery front. A row is [L, dL, da, db] in Oklab: the dark gray fur (L 0.49) gets 0.06 more lightness and moves toward blue, and the cream belly (L 0.87) moves toward blue. The gallery front then has the fur at L 0.486 and chroma 0.035, and the belly at L 0.802 and chroma 0.044. On the stage of the play frame, the fur looks neutral gray. The paws and the whiskers keep their colors, and the pink nose and inner ears have more chroma than 0.034 (docs/research/2026-10-16-cat-seat/).

belly.note: The light belly patch is an even oval in the front plane of the stretched trunk (belly_patch() of tools/blender/rig_mesh.py). The user said "make the cat's belly more oval and smooth" on 2026-10-27. The patch of the texture has a waist below the chest, and the seat showed it as a pinch. The oval is 0.0793 u wide on each side of the middle plane (13 cm in the app), with its middle at 0.5 of the line from the hips joint to the neck joint and its ends at 0 and 1.2 of the line, so that it meets the light chest above the range with no step. Each face of the trunk front from 0.22 to 0.86 of the line takes the cream, the gray, or a mix of both by the share of its area in the oval (docs/research/2026-10-27-cat-belly.md).

colors.note: Each face takes the mean sRGB color of the texture at the samples of a grid of the given steps on the face. A face is dark when its share of samples with a linear luminance below dark is at least eyeShare, and then it takes the mean of its dark samples. Each other face takes the mean of its samples that are not dark. A dark face in the eye box (the left eye at x 0.032 to 0.084, y 0.806 to 0.833 in the front view, mirrored for the right eye) is a face of an eye: 19 faces on the left and 25 on the right (docs/research/2026-10-16-cat-mesh/head-colors.txt). A face in the nose box whose color is nearer to the nose color than to white is a face of the nose: the pink nose of the cat (19 faces at y 0.768 to 0.782, z 0.214 to 0.222) and its two dark nostrils. The box starts above the three dark faces of the mouth at y 0.752. The nose color is the mean of the pink faces. Then each face takes the nearest color of a palette of palette colors, from k-means in Oklab. The values of samples, palette, dark, and eyeShare are the values of the fox.

eyeShell.note: Each eye shell is a fan from the middle of the dark faces of the eye to at most this number of points of their edge, lifted this far (units) along the normal of the eye. pnpm studio-body finds each eye by its fan, drops the fan, and the app puts its pea eye there (design 4.5). The old eye is the dark faces and each face whose middle lies within reach times the radius of their edge, seen along the normal of the eye: 67 faces on the left and 66 on the right, with the few green faces of the irises. After the palette, the faces of the old eye take the color with the largest area in the ring of faces that share a corner with it: 50% of the area of the ring of the left eye and 41% of the right eye. Then each patch of dark faces near an old eye takes the color of its own ring. The cat has no such patch within darkReach: the nearest dark faces, the nostrils and the mouth, lie in front of the plane of the eye. The values are the values of the fox.

smooth.note: The big head of the cat hangs over its thin neck, and in the app the underside of the head faces down into the shadow of the head: a black band under the head from the back and the sides, and a thin dark line under the chin from the front. The face colors there are the cream and the gray of the fur, and a render with a flat light shows no line (docs/research/2026-10-16-cat-mesh/chin-blender.webp). So the rig smooths the source inside the box before the weights, as for the dark band at the back of the neck of the fox: the neck and the bottom of the head from the back to the front of the neck (x from -0.12 to 0.12, y from 0.65 to 0.74, behind z 0.12). The chin, the jaw, the muzzle, and the eyes stay outside the box. Each vertex inside moves 0.5 of the way to the middle of its neighbors in 12 rounds: 34 vertices, at most 0.031 units. The head height H, the head center of the holds, the seat, and the footprint stay. A box to z 0.25 also smoothed the chin and changed H from 0.339 m to 0.352 m (rig-mesh-check-cat-smooth-1.log and -2.log).

chair.note: The seat is level, and its top is the lowest point of the seated body over the seat, with no shin, foot, or tail. The half width holds the haunch of the cat (x ±0.14 before the girth factor, ±0.151 with the width 1.08). The front edge ends where the thighs, which slope down, leave the seat top at the haunch. With the leg factor 1.94168, the shins start at z 0.197 units, the front edge of the seat of the app is 15.9 cm behind the back of the knees, the thighs over the front 10 cm of the seat are 0.1 cm above the seat top, and the back of the haunch is 1.2 cm in front of the back posts (docs/research/2026-10-16-cat-trunk/seat-probe.txt). With the leg factor 1.5, the seat top stays at 0.216 units with the front edge from 0.08 to 0.1 units, and it falls 0.0013 units under the thighs with 0.11 and 0.12 units. The shins start at z 0.160 units (docs/research/2026-10-16-cat-mesh/rig-mesh-check-cat-front.log), and the front edge of the seat of the app is 9.9 cm behind the back of the knees (seat-probe-legs.txt). With the leg factor 1, the front edge was 0.08 units (rig-mesh-check-cat-chair.log). The back edge keeps the back of the haunch 1.1 cm in front of the back posts of the chair of the app, as for the red fox (1.0 cm, seat-probe-legs.txt). The back edge of -0.111 units, the edge of the leg factor 1, kept it 5.0 cm in front. The seat of the app is 0.254 m high and 0.317 m deep (0.202 m and 0.316 m with the leg factor 1.5).

crease.note: The seated bind is smoothed across the crease where the belly meets the top of each thigh (crease_relax() of tools/blender/rig_mesh.py), with the values of the fox and the rabbit (docs/decisions/2026-10-16-hip-open.md). The seam has 15 vertices, 117 vertices move, at most 5.26 cm, and no face turns over (rig-mesh-check-cat-final.log). The corrective shapes give the source back, so the standing body keeps its form.
crease.lapNote: The even oval belly met the thighs with a turn of 34 degrees between the cuts of pnpm trunk-form at the bottom of the oval (22 degrees before the oval). The second smoothing of lap reaches 4 rings up the belly front, and it fades out over 0.04 units behind the hip joints and beyond 0.07 units from the middle plane, so that the seat top and the outer hips keep their places. The turn is 12 to 13 degrees, the front keeps a gap of 0 to its hull, and no edge of the lap is over 35.5 degrees (48 before). With 8 rounds, the front had a gap of 0.05 cm to its hull. With 6 rings, a face of spine1 turned over. With 4 rings and no fade, the seat top fell 2 mm and the outer hips moved up to 8.7 cm (docs/research/2026-10-27-cat-lap.md).

sit.note: The underside of the haunch behind the hip joints goes down onto the seat in the seated bind (sit() of tools/blender/rig_mesh.py). The vertices at the root of the tail share their weight with the hips (0.45 to 0.51 of the tail), so with the values of the fox they moved by half of the drop, and the side view of the underside of the final bind stayed 5.22 cm above the seat. With root, a vertex counts its tail share only by its smoothstep from 0.7 to 0.95, so the root of the tail moves with the haunch. With no gap, a ramp of 0.015 units before the hip joints, a drop of at most 0.2 units, and 2 rounds of smoothing, the side view of the final bind was 1.93 cm above the seat at most with the hanging tail. The root of the hanging tail pulled a few vertices down and set the seat top, 0.2157 units. The curled tail does not pull them, and the seat top rose 0.8 to 1.2 cm, so top keeps it. With the curled tail of studio.tailCurl, the side view is 0.16 cm above the seat at most. With the trunk factor and the leg factor 1.94168, the seat top of the hanging tail is 0.2746 units, and the side view is 0.13 cm above the seat at most (docs/research/2026-10-16-cat-trunk/). With the leg factor 1.5, the seat is 1 mm lower, the chair 2 mm deeper, and the standing body stays within 0.248 mm of the source. The thighs 25 degrees down and the shorter, wider, and deeper trunk of 2026-10-17 put the seat top of the hanging tail at 0.2673 units, and the round back of the deeper haunch stayed 1.68 cm above the seat with 2 rounds of smoothing. With 8 rounds, the side view is 0.84 cm above the seat at most with the tail curl of 2026-10-16 (3 rounds 1.12 cm, 4 rounds 1.02 cm), and 0.58 cm with the lifted curl (docs/research/2026-10-16-cat-form/seat-fit.txt). The red fox keeps 2.0 cm. The retro values gap 0 and ramp 0.015 alone gave 5.00 cm, and the haunch ramp 0.12 to 0.2 gave 5.40 cm (pnpm rig-mesh cat --check with these values as --set variants). The corrective shapes give the source back, so the standing body keeps its form.

bind.note: Each vertex with a weight on a lower bone of the left arm (the forearm segments, the elbow and wrist helpers, the paw, and the fingers) takes the dual quaternion blend in the seated bind (bind_skin() of tools/blender/rig_mesh.py), so that the elbow and the forearm keep the round tube of cat-arms.glb. The seated bind bends each elbow by 79 degrees and turns the left paw 120 degrees (studio.bindSupination), and the linear blend put the left elbow at 0.86 and the forearm at 0.84 of the radius of the tube, so the upper arm read as a bulge between a thin elbow and a thin forearm, and the elbow as a lump (user, 2026-10-27: "the cat's arm has lumps", docs/research/2026-10-27-cat-arm.md). The bow arm keeps the linear blend: it bends further than the bind in the play, so the round inner elbow of the dual quaternion blend folded a new face in 64% of the play, and a flip of its quad left a face that folded in 3.5% (0.93 of the tube at the elbow and the forearm with the linear blend, with no paw turn). The upper arms and the trunk keep the linear blend, and the app moves the bind mesh with the linear blend in each pose.

raise.note: The shape of the raised left arm of the play (pnpm raise-fit violist --faces 1594 --side L): the upper arm turns 33.7 degrees from the bind in the mean of the play, with a spread of 2.7 degrees, and the clavicle 20 degrees. The user said "the cat's arm has lumps" on 2026-10-27. The trunk weights keep the front of the left arm root with the chest, so the raised arm of the play crushed it into a dark crease, and face 1594 at the front of the armpit folded in each play sample. In the pose of the rule, each vertex within reach of the points (8 places at the front of the root, in units of the source) moves half of the way to the place that the first segment of the upper arm gives it (follow), with a share that falls to 0 from 0.02 to 0.05 units. With 0.015 to 0.04 units, the valleys in front of the root deepened 565 cm deg from the bind in the play at 30 s and 1,577 cm deg at rest (488 and 1,387 cm deg now, docs/research/2026-10-28-cat-root2.md). The shape has its full weight within 15 degrees of the turn of the rule and none from 30 degrees: with 10 and 20 degrees, face 1594 still folded in 2.5% of the lift. At rest the shape has no weight, so the root keeps the trunk weights: with no trunk weight, 11 faces folded at the root at rest and in the play, and the right root had a notch at rest (docs/research/2026-10-28-cat-wall.md). A share of 0.75 left a light notch at the lower end of the crease, a follow of the clavicle made the crease narrower and harder, and a smoothing of the skin in the pose of the rule turned over the thin faces at the front end of the armpit line, which showed as a slit (docs/research/2026-10-28-cat-root.md). After the clean of that band (step_clean_pit() of tools/blender/cat_arms.py), the smoothing still pulled the root front into a dark pocket (docs/research/2026-10-28-cat-root2.md).

The shape of the left arm at rest (pnpm raise-fit violist --faces 2255,2241,2242,2243 --side L --sets rest): the upper arm turns 75.6 degrees from the bind in the mean of the rest, with a spread of 0.9 degrees, and the clavicle does not turn. At rest the arm hangs down past the front of the root, which keeps the trunk weights, so a dark notch showed at the front of the root from az -35 to az -90, and faces 2241 to 2243, 2255, and 3845 folded in each rest sample. In the pose of the rule, the same points as in the shape of the play, with the same reach, move half of the way with the first upper arm segment. The notch is softer, and the rest folds 3 faces at most (7 before) with no new face (docs/research/2026-10-28-cat-root.md).

The shape of the left arm between the rest and the play (pnpm raise-fit violist --faces 2488,2487,3118 --side L --sets lift): the upper arm turns 55.3 degrees from the bind in the mean of the folds of the lift, with a spread of 8.2 degrees, and the clavicle 7.5 degrees. The user said "the cat's arm has lumps" on 2026-10-27. On the way from the rest to the play and back, the upper arm passes 30 to 45 degrees from the turns of the other two shapes, so they had no weight there, and the front of the root kept the crease of the trunk weights: in the lift sample 5 of boulanger-matin, the valleys in front of the root deepened 1,864 cm deg from the bind. In the pose of the rule, the same points as in the other shapes, with the same reach, move half of the way with the first upper arm segment. The shape has its full weight within 10 degrees of its turn and none from 25 degrees: with 10 to 20 degrees, the lowering samples 11 to 13 took 0.38 to 0.61 of the shape of a fit of an earlier build of the round, and now 0.70 to 0.96 (docs/research/2026-10-28-cat-root2.md).
